ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #5
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. happiness
   C. run
   D. blue

2. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension.

3. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening.

4. When practising Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension.

5. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.

6. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. No full stops
   B. Only one word repeated
   C. One main idea with supporting sentences
   D. Many unrelated topics with no link

7. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.

8. When practising Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.

9. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the Library
   B. Where is the library
   C. where is the library
   D. Where is the library?

10. When practising Writing 1.4.1 Guided Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.4.1 Guided Writing.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.4.1 Guided Writing.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Guided Writing.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.4.1 Guided Writing.

11. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a describing word
   B. Only an action
   C. Only a joining word
   D. A person, place, thing, or idea

12. When practising Pronunciation and Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Pronunciation and Listening.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Pronunciation and Listening.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Listening.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Pronunciation and Listening.

13. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

14. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goes
   B. went
   C. going
   D. goed

15. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----

25. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
